title: What a decorator is

kcs.statement: A decorator is a callable that takes a function (or class) and returns an object that is then bound to the original name.
A decorator may return the original function unchanged, after registering or annotating it, or a different callable that wraps it.

problem_ideas: Write identity(func) that returns func and confirm the decorated function behaves the same
Write a decorator that returns 42 instead of a function and predict what calling the name does
Classify five decorators as 'returns original' or 'returns replacement'
Explain why the name 'decorator' in Python differs from the GoF Decorator pattern
Write shout(func) that returns a new function upper-casing func's result
Decide whether print is a valid decorator and what the name ends up bound to
